summary: Regression after runtime upgrade (1.19.3 -> 1.20.1): increased p99 latency + occasional stream disconnects; customer requests backport into upcoming LTS instead of upgrading again
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a performance and reliability regression after upgrading their Private deployment runtime from 1.19.3 to 1.20.1. They are seeing (a) higher tail latency (p99) on chat completions and (b) intermittent streaming disconnects during long responses. Customer explicitly does not want to “chase minors” and is requesting that the suspected fix be backported into the Runtime LTS line once available.

Impact:
- Production impact for end-users: increased time-to-first-token and higher p99 end-to-end latency; some requests fail mid-stream requiring client retry.
- Customer is in a change-freeze window and wants a single, low-risk patch path (LTS) rather than another runtime minor upgrade.

Customer expectation / ask:
- Identify regression cause introduced in 1.20.x.
- Provide mitigation they can apply immediately.
- If a fix exists (or is created), backport it to runtime-1.20-lts (customer is requesting inclusion in first LTS patch once branch is cut).

Environment:
- Deployment type: Private (VPC)
- Region: us-east
- Runtime versions: 1.19.3 (good) -> 1.20.1 (bad)
- Traffic: ~55–80 RPS sustained during peak (streaming enabled)
- GPUs: A100 80GB (8x nodes), autoscaling enabled (scheduler)
- Client: Python SDK + server-sent events streaming

Observed symptoms:
1) Latency regression:
- 1.19.3: p95 ~ 1.6s, p99 ~ 3.8s (customer-reported, similar to our historical baselines)
- 1.20.1: p95 ~ 2.1s, p99 ~ 8.9s
2) Streaming disconnects:
- ~0.4–0.7% of streaming requests terminate early with client-side “unexpected EOF” / reconnect
- Server logs show downstream cancellations clustered around ~30–45s generation windows

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
- Run sustained streaming chat requests with max_tokens >= 1200 and concurrency >= 64.
- Mix of short prompts and longer system prompts; tools/function calling disabled.
- Regression visible within 10–15 minutes of load.

Logs / evidence requested:
- runtime pod logs around disconnects
- api-gateway access logs for affected request IDs
- scheduler queue depth + preemption/eviction stats
- perf dashboard screenshot comparing 1.19.3 vs 1.20.1 for the same load test

Notes:
Customer referenced prior instability with minor upgrades and asked for “risk level” tagging + fewer behavior changes per release, aligning with ongoing Runtime LTS initiative.

Will draft PR; if it lands in mainline quickly, we can evaluate backport to runtime-1.20-lts per policy.

2025-12-13 15:12 PT — Connor O'Brien (Release Eng) — Noted: runtime-1.20-lts branch cut is planned soon; backport candidates must have risk tier + evidence (perf-canary + GPU matrix). Asked support to capture a clear “customer impact statement” suitable for LTS release notes.

2025-12-16 10:21 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Update to customer:
- We believe the regression is tied to scheduler behavior changes in 1.20 under mixed-length streaming load.
- We have a mitigation that partially improves p99; full fix is being prepared.
- We will pursue an LTS backport once the fix is merged and passes regression gates; we’ll share ETA once PR is up and we have perf-canary results.
Customer asked to be included in any RC validation for the LTS patch and requested a rollback-safe upgrade procedure (we referenced the Private LTS upgrade/rollback guide draft).
resolution: Unresolved. Pending: engineering fix PR + validation. Current recommended workaround: disable scheduler preemption (where supported) and reduce per-pod streaming concurrency; customer may roll back to 1.19.3 to immediately restore baseline while fix is prepared for LTS backport consideration.
